input.content: Hi! I'm planning a trip to London.

content.text:
Welcome! I’d love to help you plan. A few quick questions to tailor it:
- When are you visiting and how long will you stay?
- What are your interests (history, art, food, shopping, nightlife, parks)?
- Is your budget comfortable for paid attractions, or do you prefer free museums and self-guided days?
- Are you traveling solo or with others?

In the meantime, here’s a concise starter plan to get you imagining London highlights.

Easy 3-day classic itinerary
- Day 1: Westminster & South Bank
  - Buckingham Palace and St James’s Park
  - Houses of Parliament, Big Ben, Westminster Abbey
  - Walk along Whitehall to Trafalgar Square
  - Optional: National Gallery or a ride on the London Eye
  - Evening in Covent Garden or along the South Bank (bite to eat, river views)

- Day 2: Museums & the South Bank vibe
  - Choose one: British Museum (Bloomsbury) or Victoria and Albert Museum (South Kensington)
  - Afternoon: Tate Modern or Shakespeare’s Globe, Millennium Bridge
  - Optional: Borough Market for food + a stroll along the Thames

- Day 3: Historic East or Greenwich
  - Tower of London and Tower Bridge (outer views are great)
  - If you love markets/streets, go to Shoreditch/Brick Lane for street art and bites
  - Alternatively, take a riverboat to Greenwich: Royal Observatory and Maritime Museum, or Charles Greenwich Park

Transport tips
- Get around with an Oyster card or contactless payment; Zone 1–2 covers most sights.
- Walking is often quicker than short Tube rides in central areas.
- Consider a 2- to 3-day Travelcard if you’ll use Tube/bus a lot.
- River services ( Thames Clippers) are a scenic travel option between central spots.

Must-know tips
- Free essentials: many museums are free (British Museum, National Gallery, Tate Britain, Victoria and Albert), with paid special exhibitions.
- Book in advance for popular attractions (Tower of London, London Eye, West End shows).
- Weather: London is notorious for variable rain—carry a compact umbrella and layers.
- Power: UK plugs are type G; bring a small adapter if needed.
- Food: try a Sunday roast, fish and chips, and coffee culture around Notting Hill, Covent Garden, or Shoreditch.

Would you like me to tailor this to your exact dates, interests, and pace? I can also fetch the current London weather and give you a day-by-day plan with times and restaurant suggestions.

Yes. It’s wise to bring a compact umbrella or a light rain jacket. London weather is variable and showers can pop up even if it looks a bit cloudy now.

Tips:
- Pack a small, packable umbrella or a thin waterproof layer with a hood.
- You can buy an inexpensive umbrella on arrival if you don’t want to pack one.
- Plan some indoor options (museums, galleries, markets) in case of rain.
